SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (regional investment protection framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act 1 of 2017 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended (sections 1, 11, 22A, 23); Companies Regulations, 2011 (GNR 351 of 28 April 2011), Regulation 13; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing Protocol effective 1 April 2023; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA); Prevention of Organised Crime Act 121 of 1998 (POCA); Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA); FIC Guidance Notes on PEPs and accountable institutions (Directive 9 and Guidance Note 3A).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or civil registry of the founder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Director's Consent to Act in Form CoR27.1
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: South African notary public (for foreign signatories, notarially attested abroad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for foreign-executed documents) or domestic notarial attestation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds confirmation for initial capital contribution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory classification as Medium_Risk_Enhanced due to non-face-to-face CMRA activity, cross-border UBOs, and digital payment rails (Stripe Recurring and credit card). Protocol requires: (i) identification and verification of all directors, officers, and UBOs at or above the 5% FICA statutory threshold; (ii) screening against the FIC published lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the domestic terrorist-related list under POCDATARA, and the EU consolidated sanctions list; (iii) mandatory OFAC SDN screening because the target payment rails involve US-dollar clearing, US payment processors, and a US nexus; (iv) domestic and foreign PEP determination with enhanced due diligence, corroborated source-of-funds, and senior-management sign-off per FIC Guidance; (v) negative-media and adverse-information checks on all UBOs; and (vi) ongoing transaction monitoring and annual re-screening under FICA section 28A.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services portal (e-CIP) of the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, https://eservices.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed in Roman script; South Africa's eleven official languages are permissible, but CIPC operational practice favors English or Afrikaans renderings for clarity and due diligence. Any name in a non-Latin script or foreign language must be accompanied by a romanized transliteration and an English rendering registered in the Memorandum of Incorporation. The full name must contain the expression 'Proprietary Limited' or the approved abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd' as the legal form suffix, and must not be offensive, misleading, or contravene section 11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a CIPC name-refusal notice via the e-CIP portal, the applicant may: (1) resubmit the same name with corrective documentation or reserve an alternative name under Regulation 13 of the Companies Regulations 2011; (2) file an objection or application for reconsideration with the Companies Tribunal within 20 business days of the refusal, invoking section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 read with Regulation 153 and using Form CTR142; (3) where the refusal rests on an administrative-law defect, pursue judicial review in the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000. For names rejected on sensitive-token or public-interest grounds, the applicant must first obtain the requisite prior written authorization or ministerial consent (e.g., FSCA consent for financial-sector tokens, or state-authority consent for state-implying tokens) before any resubmission. A reserved name may be extended once for a further period not exceeding six months upon timely application to CIPC.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible: CIPC accepts a virtual or serviced-office physical street address as the registered office of a (Pty) Ltd, provided it is a South African physical address where legal process and correspondence can be served; PO Box addresses are expressly invalid under section 23(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. For this CMRA/mail-scanning venture, the registered office may be its own operational virtual-office premises or a third-party serviced-office address, subject to POPIA compliance for scanned correspondence, FIC client due diligence record-keeping, and a demonstrable compliance nexus between the registered office, the FIC accountable-institution registration, and the Information Regulator registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 40% annual baseline probability of an unannounced physical inspection. Drivers: the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier assigned to this CMRA/virtual-office model; FIC risk-based supervision under FICA section 45A; active POPIA enforcement by the Information Regulator; and CIPC registered-office verification visits. The probability is elevated during the first 12 months of operation for a newly incorporated accountable institution using digital non-face-to-face onboarding and cross-border UBOs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 13(1), 14(1), 19, 23; Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (as enacted); Companies Regulations, 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum issued share capital is prescribed by the Companies Act; no escrow account is required. The company must issue at least one share to a member and state its authorised capital in the MOI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers' share subscription be and is hereby accepted and that one ordinary share be allotted to the first named subscriber upon payment of the par value thereof; that the registered office of the company be established at [registered address], South Africa, and that the Company Secretary be authorised to file the Notice of Incorporation and MOI with CIPC; that [Name] be appointed as sole Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Authorised Representative to open bank accounts and sign statutory returns; and that all actions already taken to incorporate the company are hereby ratified. Officers are vested with full authority to obtain licences and registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the CIPC e-Services portal, navigate to 'Company Registration', select 'Name Reservation', file Form CoR 9.1 with up to four proposed names, pay the prescribed name reservation fee, and record the transaction reference. The reservation is valid for 60 business days.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of passport or identity document for each subscriber
Proof of residential address of each subscriber if the name is less-distinctive
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or confusingly similar, file a fresh CoR 9.1 with alternative names within 10 business days, or apply to CIPC for reconsideration under Companies Regulation 9(2).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Independent incorporation practitioner / Commissioner of Oaths
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI following the prescribed format, setting out share classes, authorised share capital, directors' powers, and board composition. Every subscriber must affix a signature in the presence of a Commissioner of Oaths, and a notarial acknowledgement may be required if any subscriber is a legal person.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation draft in Form CoR 15.1A format
Subscriber consent forms and subscribed signatories
Certified identity documents or registration documents of subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC later queries a defect in the MOI, correct the document and re-execute with proper witnesses; a supplementary filing under Companies Regulation 15(2) is accepted as a cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Notice of Incorporation and Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file CoR 14.1 electronically, attaching the signed MOI and the applicant's identity document. Pay the applicable incorporation fee via the e-Services payment gateway. CIPC will issue an electronic Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 signed by every subscriber or authorised agent
Signed and witnessed Memorandum of Incorporation
Notice of registered office confirmation (Form CoR 14.1 Annexure)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query, respond through the e-Services portal within 20 business days with corrected information. If registration is rejected, re-file CoR 14.1 after rectifying the anomalies; no additional fee is payable for the first re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration and Statutory Employer Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) and Department of Employment and Labour (DEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through SARS eFiling for an income tax reference number, provisional taxpayer registration, VAT registration (compulsory if projected turnover exceeds R1 million per year), and PAYE/UIF/SDL as an employer. Register separately with the Unemployment Insurance Fund and the Compensation Fund through the applicable DEL portals.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by CIPC
Authorised representative identity document and SARS ITR form
Proof of bank account (for refund purposes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the application, submit a corrected ITR and supporting identity or address documentation; escalate to SARS branch if electronic verification fails. DEL registrations can be reinstated upon submission of a labour registration form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Board Ratification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first physical or virtual board meeting to ratify all incorporation actions and adopt the bank mandate. Submit the certificate of incorporation, MOI, board resolution, and full beneficial ownership information to the chosen bank to open a currency and operating account. Link the payment rails (Stripe recurring, credit card) to the new corporate account.
required_dossiers: Certified board resolution on bank mandate
Directors' identity documents and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank flags a FICA deficiency, provide source-of-funds details and an updated beneficial ownership declaration; if rejected, appeal to the bank's compliance committee or open an account with another registered bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Communications and Digital Technologies – Postal Services Division; and the relevant Metropolitan Municipality under the Business Act 71 of 1991
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Postal Activity Exemption/Registration (Postal Services Act 124 of 1998) and Municipal Business Licence for Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) Activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) – Environmental Impact Assessment Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (No Listed Activity under GN R327 EIA Regulations, 2014) – Restricted to Category 3 Low-Potential Waste Generation; no Full EIA Report required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero point-source liquid discharge; no VOC-emitting printing, chemical, or fuel processes; paper and cardboard waste must be recycled or disposed through a municipal licensed waste stream; no hazardous waste storage exceeding 25 kg on a single site; shredder oil and electronic waste handled as controlled waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the local fire department; electrical Certificate of Compliance (CoC) for the work premises; Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 compliance inspection including workstation floor-space (minimum 2.5 m² per worker), first-aid kit, fire extinguisher servicing, and a documented emergency evacuation plan approved by the Inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling portal at www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity or a South African (Pty) Ltd carrying on enterprise activities must first register with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) where applicable, then obtain an Income Tax Reference Number through SARS eFiling within 60 days of commencing business or becoming liable for tax. VAT registration must be submitted electronically via SARS eFiling using Form VAT101 within 21 days of exceeding the compulsory R1 million taxable-supplies threshold, or immediately when voluntary registration is sought. Foreign entities without a South African permanent establishment or physical presence may only require registration for VAT on imported digital services or specific withholding obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or pass-through election exists. Statutory elections available to a (Pty) Ltd include the VAT group registration election under s50 of the VAT Act, corporate restructure rollover relief under s45 and s47 of the Income Tax Act, dividend withholding tax concession elections, and hybrid mismatch disallowance under s23M. All elections are made by formal notice to SARS through eFiling and require prescribed supporting documentation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 compulsory turnover threshold in any 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted where taxable supplies exceed R50,000 in the preceding 12 months
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, central e-invoicing validation, or digital stamping. SARS requires full tax invoices with all statutory particulars and permits electronic invoicing via accredited platforms. SARS has published a draft e-invoicing strategy and is gradually implementing an e-invoicing exchange, but no mandatory real-time clearance or VAT crypto-certificate regime is in force as of the current tax period. Vendors must retain all e-invoice source documents for at least five years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exported goods applies under s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where the supplier exports the movable goods in the course of the supply and retains prescribed documentary proof of export. Services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated under s11(2)(l) where the services are supplied directly in connection with land or movable property situated outside South Africa, or where the services are not supplied directly in connection with South African land or movable property and are supplied to a non-resident. For the virtual office and mail scanning service, the supplier must evidence that the recipient is a non-resident and that the services are not connected with South African situs assets to claim 0% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) containing the unique export clearance reference
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing actual export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange receipt demonstrating payment from outside South Africa
Commercial invoice with VAT zero-rating indicator and total consideration in foreign currency
Service agreement or contract identifying the non-resident recipient and the offshore nature of the service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may retrospectively disallow zero-rating and claw back VAT refunds if documentary proof is not contemporaneous and complete. Understatement penalties can reach up to 150% of the assessed shortfall under the Tax Administration Act, interest is imposed on underpayments, and fraudulent zero-rating claims may trigger criminal prosecution for tax evasion with fines and imprisonment. Refund claims are subject to SARS verification, field audits, and enhanced due diligence before payment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), exercising exchange control authority delegated by the National Treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is extensively convertible for current account transactions (trade and non-trade) subject to documentary verification by Authorised Dealers. Capital account transactions, including foreign equity injections and certain intercompany funding structures, require FinSurv approval or are governed by specific limits. Profit and dividend remittances to non-residents are permitted after full South African Income Tax and Dividend Withholding Tax compliance, via an Authorised Dealer, upon presentation of a valid SARS Tax Clearance Certificate (TAXCOM) and proof of the onshore source of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual, export proceeds from services rendered (including CMRA digital mail scanning contracts) must be received within 180 days from date of invoice or date of shipment as applicable. No mandatory percentage of export receipt conversion to ZAR is imposed; the exporter may retain proceeds in an approved foreign currency account with an Authorised Dealer, but full repatriation into a South African bank account is required within the prescribed timeline. Late receipt or any deviation requires FinSurv consent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (ZAR); Foreign Currency Account available

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-high feasibility for collecting foreign subscription fees via offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Wise and Payoneer; these can serve as acceptable front-end collection rails for low-value recurring transactions. However, EMIs are not Authorised Dealers under SARB exchange control and cannot issue ZAR-denominated accounts; all received funds must ultimately be repatriated through a licensed South African bank. Legal constraints include FIC Act reporting, EMIs must hold a valid license in their home jurisdiction, and any EMI account balances must be declared to SA banking compliance to avoid circumvention of the 180-day repatriation rule.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Standard South African bank practice requires at least one director or an authorized signatory to attend a physical in-person KYC interview during the account on-boarding process. Limited remote on-boarding is permitted for locally resident directors with advanced eKYC platforms, but for foreign nationals or majority non-resident-owned companies a physical visit or an attended interview at a South African bank branch is effectively mandatory. Some banks (e.g., Standard Bank) accept digital video interviews with notarized and apostilled identity documents, but not as a purely remote alternative without any physical touchpoint.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity operating as a virtual office/mail scanning CMRA with no visible physical operational site or local staff
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client service contracts; CMRA licensing confirmation from the South African Post Office (SAPO) or relevant municipal/institutional registration; commercial virtual office lease; ICT system audit documentation for digital scanning; detailed business continuity plan; valid SARS Tax Clearance Certificate; annual financial statements; undertaking for physical site inspection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and cross-border merchant payment inflows via Stripe and credit cards creating an enhanced-AML profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and proof of residential address for all directors and beneficial owners; source-of-wealth declaration; substantiated capital introduction details; Stripe merchant agreement and consolidated payment analytics; live wire-test statements; full cash-flow traceability; Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Counter-Financing of Terrorism (CFT) policy; Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) registration confirmation as an Accountable Institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium-risk enhanced due diligence resulting from ISIC 8299 business-support industry classification and high subscription volume with high-risk jurisdiction exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FIC Risk and Compliance Return (RCR) acknowledgment; comprehensive Customer Due Diligence (CDD) matrix; beneficial ownership register; automated transaction monitoring rules; force-currency screening evidence; cash threshold reporting logs; compliance officer's signed attestation; detailed business case demonstrating legitimate CMRA subscription model.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity capital must be introduced via SWIFT MT103 payment with the explicit reference 'ZA_PTY share subscription' and routed through an Authorised Dealer. The Authorised Dealer must receive a Secure Payment Form (SPF), the CSD form (for share allotment), a notarized board resolution, the amended Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI), and a share register update as evidence. Non-resident shareholder loan injections require an intercompany loan agreement and must be disclosed to FinSurv; all inbound amounts are subject to FICA verification and may be intermediately held on a Capital Escrow Account before allocation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-related disbursements for service contracts, foreign subcontractors, software subscriptions, and physical mail postage are typically settled through SWIFT MT103 payments using relevant SARB-CEM purpose codes (e.g., 8100 for professional services, 7100 for postage, or 3210 for software licensing). Higher-value or term-based hardware/software purchases may be structured through irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit incorporating UCP 600 rules; all outgoing remittances must be reported via an Authorised Dealer and remain subject to underlying export/import documentation requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX Forwards with a maximum tenor of 12 months for ZAR/USD or ZAR/EUR trade receivables
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) referencing ZAR as the anchor currency
Cross-Currency Swaps for documented commercial exposures subject to FinSurv pre-approval
Option collars and zero-cost strangles available through Authorised Dealers when capacity to settle is evidenced

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, s. 33; statutory fee ZAR 1,175 for the lowest turnover tier)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation; CIPC permits early lodgement from 30 calendar days before the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Prescribed late-filing penalties apply according to turnover tier and delay period (approximately ZAR 145 - ZAR 1,455); CIPC e-services and good-standing certificates are blocked while returns are overdue; failure to file annual returns or pay prescribed fees for two consecutive years triggers administrative deregistration under s. 82(3) of the Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Lodgement of Securities Register and Beneficial Ownership Register (CIPC annual confirmation; no separate CIPC fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, aligned with the annual return cycle (within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary); any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be lodged with CIPC within 30 business days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate CIPC fee currently prescribed for the annual lodgement; maintenance or lodgement failures constitute an administrative contravention under the Companies Act, exposing the company to compliance notices and penalties, blocking CIPC transactional services, and potentially contributing to deregistration proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is compulsory where the public interest score (PIS) is 350 or more; where the company is a public company, state-owned company, or otherwise subject to an audit requirement under the Companies Act or sectoral regulation; or where the annual financial statements are not prepared in accordance with IFRS or IFRS for SMEs. A private company with a PIS of 100 - 349 must obtain an independent review; a PIS below 100 carries no statutory audit or review obligation unless the memorandum of incorporation or shareholders resolve otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS applies where the company's PIS is 350 or more, where its securities are publicly traded, or where its financial statements are consolidated; IFRS for SMEs is available to all other qualifying companies. Annual financial statements must present fairly and comply with s. 29 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 and the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024, the company must maintain a securities register and a register of beneficial ownership and lodge a copy with CIPC at least once per calendar year, on the annual return cycle. Every transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded promptly and filed within the prescribed 30-business-day update period. The annual lodgement operates as the board-confirmed annual confirmation, and the registers must remain accurate and available for regulatory inspection.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120-350 per annum (typical South African market range for a registered office or corporate secretarial agent, commonly bundled with mail scanning and virtual office services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000-6,000 per annum for a certified statutory audit of a small private company; USD 800-2,500 per annum for an independent review where no audit is mandatory

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) submitted electronically via SARS eFiling; provisional returns via IRP6
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 must be filed within 12 months of the financial year-end; SARS may impose a shorter period in the Notice of Assessment/Completion. Provisional tax: 1st IRP6 within 6 months of the start of the year of assessment; 2nd IRP6 no later than the last day of the year of assessment; optional 3rd top-up within 6 months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification, financial year-end, registration and contact details, trade classification (ISIC 8299), PAYE/UIF/SDL reference numbers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide South African SARS tax reference number, local registered office and postal address; no foreign address may serve as the sole registered address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and statement of profit or loss: turnover from virtual office and mail scanning fees; cost of sales; operating expenses (software subscriptions, cloud storage, scanning equipment depreciation, credit card and Stripe processing fees, rent, salaries)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accounts must be prepared in ZAR under IFRS or a SA-CA(SA) approved framework; expenses paid cross-border must be identified with associated section 31 transfer pricing disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation: gross income lines (service fees, ancillary income), exempt income (foreign dividends if applicable), section 11(a) general deduction, section 11(d) bad debts, section 11(e) wear-and-tear (scanning hardware, computers, office equipment)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If revenue is earned from offshore clients, disclose foreign derivation; apportionment of expenses must follow section 11(a) read with section 23 of the ITA; treaty permanent establishment exposure abroad to be assessed separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains and losses: inclusion rate 80% for companies. Gains or losses on disposal of capital assets (office leases, equipment, goodwill)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not taxable on South African CGT unless they hold a 20% or greater interest in the company (that taxable for indirect asset disposal); the company itself remains fully taxable on its own capital gains.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening assessed loss, current-year loss, set-off, closing assessed loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indefinite carryforward, but if the company is 100% foreign-owned, consider continuity-of-trade and section 20A (loss limitation rules) which restrict loss set-off after a change of ownership/trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income × 27%; calculation of credits (foreign tax credits under s6quat), provisional tax payments offset, final liability or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits on cross-border service income must be supported by proof of foreign tax paid; DTA residence certificate may be required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by director or public officer that the return is true and complete
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The public officer (a South African resident) must sign; non-resident directors should appoint a public officer as required under s246 TAA.
